Documentation → Releases → 2.9.0

SATOM 2.9.0

Every action you take on a device now runs as a background job that shows its progress, and writes to the same device queue instead of colliding.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
On this page
  • In short
  • What's new
  • Every device action runs as a job
  • Fast actions stay fast
  • See where an action is
  • Writes to the same device wait their turn
  • Jobs on this device
  • Discovery and rediscovery are jobs too
  • What changes for you
  • Fixed
  • Learn more

Released: 2026-10-02 · All releases

In short#

This release changes how SATOM carries out anything you do to an appliance. Instead of a button that freezes until a slow device answers (or times out half-way through a change), every device action now runs as a background job that shows where it is, step by step. Writes to the same device line up behind each other. Operators who work on many devices or slow appliances will notice it most. It also fixes a large number of buttons that looked like plain text.

What's new#

Every device action runs as a job#

The request was simple: every action inside a device should create a job, run in the background and show how far it has got. Until now, an action that talked to an appliance ran while your browser waited. A slow appliance meant a frozen button and no feedback, and if it took too long the request was cut off with the device possibly half-changed. Only a handful of device actions used jobs.

Now almost every action in the device areas runs as a job, including:

  • appliances, Workspace, the object editor and the server policy wizard;
  • Web Protection, Server Objects, Exceptions and the Certificate Manager;
  • templates and change requests;
  • FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator pages;
  • attack search, the transaction tracer, Lua studio and the API explorer;
  • provisioning, the upgrade flow, Sentinel and monitors.

Sign-in, permissions and ADOM/device checks apply exactly as before, and no page looks different.

Fast actions stay fast#

SATOM waits about two seconds for the action to finish.

  • If it finishes in that time, you get the normal result, as before.
  • If it takes longer, the action is handed to a job right away. On pages that update in place, the job notice follows it and the page gets its normal result when it is done. On classic forms you are taken to a progress page that switches to the action's own result page when it finishes. Confirmation messages are kept.

See where an action is#

Each call SATOM makes to the appliance, and each SSH command, is one step of the job, shown with its result and how long it took. You can follow the steps in the job notice, on the progress page and in the job's details on the Jobs page.

Writes to the same device wait their turn#

  • Two changes to the same device run one after the other. The second one shows Queued — waiting for the first action, and you can stop it while it waits.
  • Once a change has started on the device it can no longer be stopped: stopping between two calls would leave the device half-changed.
  • Read-only actions never queue, and can be stopped between calls.

Jobs on this device#

The appliance page now lists the running and recent jobs for that device, and refreshes as soon as one starts or ends.

Discovery and rediscovery are jobs too#

A discovery or rediscovery now appears in the jobs dock and on the Jobs page with its progress. You can stop it from either place, or from the Discovery page as before.

What changes for you#

  • Device actions that take more than a moment now show progress instead of a frozen button.
  • The Jobs page stays readable: an action that never reached a device (for example a form error, or an edit that only changes SATOM's own database) does not leave a job behind.
  • Some things deliberately work as before: calls made with API tokens, actions on the standby node, and the actions that were already jobs (firmware upgrade and downgrade, backups, signature sync, monitor sweeps). Administrators can turn the new behaviour off with a node setting.

Fixed#

  • 93 buttons looked like plain text. Buttons such as Edit, Analysis / FortiView and most quick actions on the appliance page had no background or border. They now look like buttons again, and a new check stops this from coming back.
  • The update package builder could not be run directly. On a fresh copy of the source, running the script that builds an offline update package failed with Permission denied unless you started it through the shell explicitly. It now runs directly. Nothing inside an update package or an installed node changes.
